sources.title: Beatrice Leal: Arts of the Abbasid Caliphate
sources.note: Scholarly essay, 19 December 2021. Direct fetch failed; full indexed original returned via site.smarthistory.org/arts-abbasid-caliphate "750" "revolution". Opening and Cities sections; no claim that the entire caliphate stayed centrally governed.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Art of the Abbasid period, 750 to 1258
sources.note: Direct essay by Suzan Yalman based on Linda Komaroff, 2001. Samarra 836 to 892, Buyid/Seljuq captures, Mustansiriyya 1228 to 1233, 1258 conquest and later nominal Egyptian caliphs.

sources.title: Peter J. Brown and Maaike van Berkel: Water provision in early Islamic cities (2024)
sources.note: Direct full scholarly chapter, section 6, Residential Water Supply and Commercial Involvement. Samarra paragraph and printed pp.94 to 95: water carriers, courtyard features, bitumen and private baths, sampled houses not connected to a city-wide supply.

sources.title: Nawal Nasrallah: Arabic medieval cookbooks in English translation
sources.note: Direct ASOR Ancient Near East Today article, May 2019, by translator of the source. Opening al-Warraq section only: wealthy patron, tenth-century Baghdad, 620+ recipes, handwashing/table manners and Helsinki manuscript sandwich caption. Later Egyptian recipes not transferred to Abbasids.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Polychrome luster tile fragment, 23.75.25
sources.note: Full indexed collection catalogue: ninth century, excavated Samarra, two firings, metallic pigment and polish, imitation of semiprecious stone.

sources.title: University of St Andrews MacTutor: Al-Khwarizmi
sources.note: Direct scholarly biography by J. J. O’Connor and E. F. Robertson. Quoted author preface on practical calculation, six equation forms, all-verbal presentation and completing-square example. No claim he invented all algebra.

sources.title: US National Library of Medicine: Arabic legacies
sources.note: Direct institutional manuscript exhibition, Arabic Legacies section: Muslim, Jewish and Christian collaborators, paper, Hunayn workshop, Questions on Medicine and later textbooks.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Science and the art of the Islamic world, educator resource
sources.note: Direct PDF, printed p.100/PDF p.10: pharmacy family apprenticeship, imagined medicine-preparing scene in 1224 manuscript, attribution Baghdad or northern Jazira. Avoid universal access or efficacy claims and do not adopt broad House-of-Wisdom simplification.

sources.title: British Museum: Tombstone of Ya’qub ibn ‘Abdullah, 859
sources.note: Direct collection text, museum 1891,0701.1, marble found/acquired Egypt, AH244/859; exact Arabic opening and English translation in Inscriptions. Display is modern Unicode transcription of Kufic carving.

proposedOverrides.name: Abbasid Caliphate
proposedOverrides.summary: The Iraq-centred Abbasid dynasty linked imperial government, urban crafts and scholarship; its Baghdad rule ended in 1258 after centuries of changing regional power.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Existing indexed dynasty only; no aliases/new boundaries.
batchIdentityNotes.mapDates: Historical index750 to 1258; actual decoded polygon snapshots only800 to 900 and900 to 1000. Narrative explicitly distinguishes geographic coverage and dynasty lifetime.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: Baghdad/Samarra polity ending1258; Egyptian ceremonial continuation explained, not treated as unchanged empire. Early outlines cannot imply direct uniform control; later caliphal prestige versus Buyid/Seljuq armies differentiated.
batchIdentityNotes.geometryStatus: Imported outlines retained, no correction certified. Existing generic Mongol successor link cleared in proposal because recipient geometry at1258 not audited; conquest stated explicitly in prose.
